problem: The displacement $s$ (in meters) relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by $s(t)={e}^{{t}^{2}-4t+6}$, where $t\ge 0$ is the time measured in seconds. Find the time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of decreasing $x.$

feedback.problem: The displacement $s$ (in meters) relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by $s(t)=(4t-7){e}^{t}$, where $t\ge 0$ is the time measured in seconds. Determine the time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of increasing $x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
If the particle moves in the direction of increasing $x,$ then its velocity is positive.

First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((4t-7){e}^{t}) \\  & =(4t-3){e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of increasing $x$, we solve $v(t)>0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & >0 \\ (4t-3){e}^{t} & >0 \\ 4t-3 & >0 \\ t & >\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the time interval in which the particle is moving to the direction of increasing $x$ is $(\frac{3}{4},\infty ).$
